Aaron C. Guckian

Republican candidate for Governor, Rhode Island · Open seat

Former executive director of the Rhode Island Dental Association; has also worked in banking, nonprofit fundraising and teaching

Aaron Guckian is a Republican from East Greenwich and the Republican nominee for governor of Rhode Island in 2026. He ran unsuccessfully for lieutenant governor in 2022 and announced his run for governor on December 1, 2025. He ran against Elaine Pelino in the Republican primary, and on November 3 he faces Democrat Helena Buonanno Foulkes and independent Ken Block, among others.

Where Guckian stands

Housing
Opposes Foulkes' plan to build housing with money from a tax on millionaires, saying more spending does not work. Proposes a veterans' housing village and a 'permitting czar' to cut red tape.
Housing mandates
Supports cutting red tape that holds back affordable housing. Says he does not believe in state mandates.
Taxes
Proposes repealing the so-called 'Taylor Swift tax' on second homes.
Truck tolls
Opposes bringing back Rhode Island's truck tolls.
Energy
Proposes working with the Trump administration on advanced energy, including a commission to study fusion and small modular reactors. Calls for building a new natural gas pipeline right away.
Federal relations
Says he is the only candidate who can bring in federal money, because he would work with the Trump administration.
State spending
Proposes a 'Rhode Island Works Smarter' plan to reduce state spending. It would have frontline and union workers identify savings and would speed up permitting.
Surveillance cameras
Has raised concerns about Flock license plate cameras used by police, but has not called for shutting them off.

Background

  • Republican nominee for Governor of Rhode Island, 2026
  • Republican candidate for Lieutenant Governor of Rhode Island, 2022 (lost)
  • Executive director, Rhode Island Dental Association (stepped down before the 2026 campaign)
  • Head of fundraising, Rhode Island Foundation
  • Several jobs in banking
  • Music teacher, North Kingstown High School; former opera singer
  • Aide to Rhode Island's last Republican governor
  • Played college basketball; East Greenwich native
